result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a wide, unmarked commercial driveway that interrupts the sidewalk, creating a significant conflict zone. The lack of marked crosswalks, pedestrian signage, and poor roadway pavement quality further degrades the safety of the walking environment.

hazards.name: Wide Unmarked Driveway
hazards.description: A wide commercial entrance lacks markings to define pedestrian priority, creating a large area of exposure for people walking along the sidewalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the image, crossing the sidewalk path.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: The walls flanking the driveway entrance block the view between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers exiting the facility.
hazards.location_in_image: Walls on the left and right sides of the driveway entrance.

hazards.name: Degraded Roadway Surface
hazards.description: Cracked and patched pavement in the foreground creates tripping hazards and uneven surfaces for anyone attempting to cross the street.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Driveway Markings
interventions.description: Paint a high-visibility crosswalk across the driveway to clearly delineate the pedestrian path and reinforce right-of-way.

interventions.title: Daylighting and Sightline Improvements
interventions.description: Modify or lower the walls at the driveway entrance to ensure drivers and pedestrians can see each other before a conflict occurs.

interventions.title: Raised Pedestrian Crossing
interventions.description: Install a raised sidewalk across the driveway to force vehicles to slow down and maintain the pedestrian level.

result.summary: The image depicts a residential intersection with basic pedestrian infrastructure, including sidewalks and a marked zebra crosswalk. However, the crosswalk markings are significantly faded, and there is a lack of dedicated pedestrian signals or traffic calming measures to protect vulnerable road users.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The zebra-style crosswalk markings are heavily worn and faded, reducing their visibility to approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground across the main roadway.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles close to the intersection corner may obstruct the view between pedestrians waiting to cross and oncoming traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Left and right curbsides near the intersection.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Repaint the crosswalk with high-visibility thermoplastic markings to improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten the crossing distance and improve sightlines by preventing parking too close to the corner.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear information on when it is safe to cross.

result.summary: The intersection is equipped with basic pedestrian infrastructure including marked zebra crosswalks, curb ramps, and signalized control. However, the presence of parked vehicles near the corners and the lack of physical traffic calming measures like curb extensions may reduce visibility and increase pedestrian exposure.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the intersection corners block sightlines between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curbs approaching the intersection on both sides of the street.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces closest to the intersection to ensure clear sightlines for all road users.

result.summary: The image shows a signalized intersection with sidewalks but lacking marked crosswalks and pedestrian signals. The roadway is relatively wide with a painted bike lane, creating an environment that prioritizes vehicular flow over pedestrian safety.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crosswalk
hazards.description: There are no painted crosswalks at this signalized intersection, making pedestrian crossing points unclear to drivers.

hazards.name: Missing Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No pedestrian-specific signal heads are visible, leaving pedestrians to rely on vehicular signals which may not provide adequate clearance time.

hazards.name: Sight Line Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles near the intersection corners may block the view between pedestrians waiting to cross and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the street near the intersection

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental or ladder-style marked crosswalks on all legs of the intersection to clearly define pedestrian space.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear information on crossing time and improve safety.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct curb extensions (bulb-outs) to shorten the crossing distance and improve sight lines between pedestrians and drivers.
